study_notes.title: Light and Heat: The Bulb Anatomy

the_bulb.visual_reference: [IMAGE_017: Detailed labeled diagram of a light bulb]
the_bulb.Filament: Coiled wire made of Tungsten (Wolfram). High melting point and high resistance.
the_bulb.Inert_Gases: Argon and Nitrogen protect the filament from oxygen so it doesn't burn out.
the_bulb.Glass_Envelope: Hold gases and allows light to pass.
the_bulb.Cement: Holds the glass to the brass cap.

the_torch.visual_reference: [IMAGE_018: X-ray view of a torch showing internal path]
the_torch.Reflector: Reflects light into a parallel focused beam.
the_torch.Tail_Spring: Ensures the cells have firm contact and completes the circuit to the metal body.
the_torch.Casing_Faults: A rusted casing acts as an insulator and stops the torch from working.

IMAGE_017.description: A bulb with arrows pointing to the coiled tungsten, the inert gas space, and the brass base.

IMAGE_018.description: A side view of a torch showing three batteries in a row, the spring at the back, and the reflector at the front.
